HONEST, declared cut: the container's lifecycle (provisioning, recycling, cleanup, what survives a restart) is left for the phase with a migration slot — container state is mutable and needs a table, and a container that comes up without recycling is worse than none. Consequence: the "inside is free" half of the terminal policy has NOT changed yet; 0055 keeps holding as-is until the wall really goes up 0081 Container lifecycle: a state table, no orchestrator. Closes the cut 0065 declared about itself ("What this ADR does NOT do") — project_containers (migration 0046) records mutable STATE (status, image_version pointing at the Architect's decision without duplicating it, container_id, DECLARED resource caps, failure_reason), one row per project like dev_agent_states in the engine (0045), with a pure state machine (provisioning → running ⇄ stopped, failed reachable from all three, removed only exits by reprovisioning) in the same shape as session-state-machine.ts. Prior investigation confirmed NO product service mounts /var/run/docker.sock or runs privileged — and that's why the two use cases (Registrar/ObterCicloDeVidaDoContainer) only WRITE and READ, no real Docker call: mounting the socket to "actually make it work" would be a security decision (a root-escalation vector) nobody asked for in this slice. The first transition (provisioning) requires the image already decided (RN-105, same gate as the Code tab) and FREEZES version/resources onto the row; a project in workspace_mode: 'local' (0072) is refused, because it doesn't stand up its own container. No new HTTP route — with no real consumer yet, exposing one would be guessing a contract 0083 The Terminal tab gets the lifecycle's real consumer, not the terminal itself. Revises the part of 0081 that deferred the HTTP route until a real consumer existed — this piece (PROGRAM 28, Wave 5/F2) was that consumer. The original plan was the full interactive terminal, but Phase 25b stays cut: no service mounts /var/run/docker.sock, and nothing in production transitions project_containers (ADR 0081 created the table, not an orchestrator). Implementing a fake terminal — or one running in the same container as the Brabo monorepo, the debt 0055 already describes as policy — would invent capability, the same mistake ADRs 0041/0042 refuse for provider and model. The real delivery: GET /projects/:projectId/container/lifecycle (RN-267), a faithful mirror of ObterCicloDeVidaDoContainerUseCase, and CodeBottomPanel.tsx showing that state (translated badge, failure reason) UNDER the explanatory text that already existed — never replacing it —, fetched only while the Terminal tab is open (RN-268). null (never provisioned) is today's honest, most common result 0128 Docker access in the runner goes behind a PORT with exactly five operations (start/stop/remove/inspect/exec), and the implementation was chosen by a PROOF that failed. dockerode was installed, imported, instantiated and exercised (ping()) through a --self-test-docker flag run against the real artifacts — never an import a bundler could tree-shake. tsup passed (it leaves dependencies as an external require, so dockerode never entered the bundle); bun build --compile (ADR 0112, the standalone binary) REPROVED, with the error recorded verbatim: Could not resolve: "../build/Release/cpufeatures.node". The chain is mandatory, not accidental — docker-modem/lib/modem.js requires ./ssh at module top level, ssh2 requires cpu-features, and that optional native binding is wrapped in a runtime try/catch the BUNDLER does not have. Same class of problem ADR 0112 documented for node-pty, with the difference that decides it: there the binding is ESSENTIAL, here it accelerates an SSH transport this runner never uses (it speaks to the local unix socket). Measured and NOT adopted, so nobody redoes the investigation: --external cpu-features compiles (280 modules against 79, +1.7 MB per binary × 5 platforms) and dockerode works inside the binary — it is exactly the creative workaround the product owner excluded in advance. So the runner uses execFile('docker', …), dockerode is gone from the lockfile, and the BROKER (PR 1.2) does not inherit the decision: it ships in an image we build and never becomes a standalone binary. Containment is the TYPE, not caller discipline: no field for privileged/cap_add, RedeDoContainer is `'none' 0130 The container BROKER is born — a new Node/TS service (apps/broker), the only process in the product that talks to a Docker daemon on the SERVER, and the api never receives the socket. Three inseparable decisions. First, the port MOVES: docker-port.ts and docker-cli.ts (and their two specs) leave apps/runner/src/ for a new workspace package, packages/docker-port, consumed by runner and broker — exactly what ADR 0128 wrote it would do, never copied, because "a second file with the same five operations and a sixth 'broker only' is the beginning of the end of containment". packages/shared was refused for the invariant it declares and packages-shared-so-tipos.spec.ts keeps honest (100% type, and the api's production image dies with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING if a runtime value survives tsc); the new package has NO build step and is BUNDLED by both consumers (tsup, bun build --compile), which is why the api cannot consume it and why validarDecisaoDeImagem does NOT move. The standalone binary survived the move, measured: build, build:bin, smoke and smoke:bin green, Bun bundle 79 → 83 modules, npm pack --dry-run unchanged. Second, and this is the point of the service: the broker does not accept a container spec. It takes a projectId plus one of the five operations, READS the Architect's decision from the api itself (GET /internal/projects/:projectId/container-spec, RN-485) and COMPOSES image, network, resources and the single mount — there is no field in which to write privileged, cap_add, network: host or a free -v, because there is no field. It revalidates what the api returned, since containment that depends on the caller being correct is not containment, and the two validations answer different questions (the api's is about the ARTIFACT being reviewable; this one is the parse of untrusted JSON into the closed type). One check exists only here and is new: an image reference starting with - would be read by the CLI as a FLAG — execFile without a shell solves command injection, not ARGUMENT injection. Third, the api sends NO path at all: -v is resolved by the daemon against the HOST filesystem, so a path from inside the api container would silently mount an empty folder; the broker joins workspaceDirName (RN-109) with its own PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT and refuses start when that is missing rather than guessing. pidsLimit joins the port for a reason worth naming — the artifact always carried three numbers and dropping one would make it promise a cap the container does not get. Contained by five independent layers: no published port, an internal: true network only the api joins, the shared service token compared in constant time, five operations, and the computed spec. It ships under profiles: ["container-broker"] in both composes and is therefore OFF by default, and its image is NOT published to the GHCR — docker-bake.hcl and ALVOS keep the four images of ADR 0119. The api gains a port and an HTTP client whose only CALLER is inspect: the container lifecycle route now returns the OBSERVED state beside the RECORDED one, never fused, with naoObservado naming why when there was no way to look (RN-486) — so the table can now lie, and the read says so. Nothing brings a container up: no loop, no queue, no container_start proposed_action, and RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase is byte-for-byte unchanged, mode guard included 0131 The Architect gains a seventh tool, route_modules_to_infra: one item {modulo, imagemCandidata, porque} per module of the CURRENT module_map, recorded as artifact.module_routing — no table, same design as artifact.module_map/artifact.project_image/artifact.c4_diagram, the event IS the artifact. The Architect only CANDIDATES; electing among the candidates (or refusing all of them) is Infra's job, in a later PR — this one only produces the auditable list. Each item's image goes through the SAME rule choose_project_image already applies (validarDecisaoDeImagem: explicit tag/digest, latest rejected, a real rationale), reused rather than reimplemented per item; the new domain (module-routing.ts) only adds what's proper to the LIST — empty is refused (not a decision), a repeated module is refused (ambiguous: which of the two images wins?), and each modulo must name one that exists in the current module_map, refused by naming the VALID ones, same rule as assign_story_modules. :direct, never proposed_action: routing has no external effect. build_kickoff/1 — the Architect's only source of tool ORDER — lists the new tool right after create_module_map 0133 ADR 0131 left half a sentence hanging — "the Architect only candidates, Infra elects, in a separate PR" — and this is that PR, wired to the other hanging sentence, in the broker's own port comment (ADR 0130): "starting is external effect and doesn't happen without a proposed_action; Infra proposes it, with the user's final authority — another PR." The join between the two exposes a question neither ADR answered: the broker takes no spec, it reads GET .../container-spec, which reads artifact.project_image (RN-105) — not artifact.module_routing. So an election that doesn't become a new version of artifact.project_image is auditable and INERT — the container that comes up is whatever choose_project_image said, unrelated to what Infra just elected. Decision: the election REUSES DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase whole, called now with decidedBy: 'infra-lead' instead of the default 'arquiteto' — same validation (validarDecisaoDeImagem, same resource ceiling), same single "current" artifact, same precedent module-routing.ts's own comment already set for reusing instead of reimplementing. The elected image MUST be one of the routing's imagemCandidata — never invented — checked before touching the artifact, refused by name with the valid candidates listed when it isn't. New container_start proposed_action (maintainer, deliberately outside the absolute-ceiling block in decide.ts, same reasoning already recorded there for propose_execution_plan/assess_implementability — first election, not a ceiling raise) is the FIRST real caller of ContainerBrokerPort.start — of the five operations ADR 0128/0130 declared, only inspect had one before. RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase gets its first non-test caller too, transitioning provisioning → running (or straight to running from stopped, since the ADR 0081 state machine refuses stopped → provisioning) only after the broker confirms. Dev agents still do not run inside the container that comes up — that's a later PR 0134 Closes what ADR 0133 left declared: "dev agents still do not run inside the container that comes up — that's a later PR." Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor.decisao_de_execucao/1 gains a FIFTH outcome, :executar_no_container — execution_mode: container with a project_containers row REGISTERED running (Engine.Containers.ProjectContainerLifecycle.running?/1, a new read-only Ecto schema mirroring Engine.Projects.Project's pattern) — and the terminal command crosses engine → api (POST internal/projects/:projectId/container-exec, a new route in InternalProjectsController, not the broker-facing InternalContainersController, since the caller here is the engine and nothing is WRITTEN to the lifecycle table) → broker (ContainerBrokerPort.exec, the last of the five ADR 0128/0130 operations to gain a real caller), running via docker exec instead of System.cmd inside the engine process. cwd, when present, is translated from the HOST path (inside PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT) to /work by the engine before the call — verified in code, not assumed: the broker's raizDoProjeto (PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT + workspaceDirName) and the engine's PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT + workspace_dir_name resolve the SAME physical directory, so Workspace.ensure!/4 needed zero changes — the container is just a second observer of the worktree the dev agent already had. A running row is only ever the REGISTERED state (RN-486: registered and observed never merge); a dead or externally-removed container turns the broker call into an ordinary failed_result — never a crash, never a silent fallback back outside the container, which would reopen the isolation gap this PR closes. Terminal actions scoped to the project's real container also gain an auto-approval FLOOR — containerExecutionActive in DecideContext, set by ProposeActionUseCase only for terminal in execution_mode: container — that changes decide()'s INITIAL value from require_approval to auto_approve; it is a floor, not a new ceiling: agent_autonomy/permissions.json can still lower it exactly as they already lower the old default, and the five absolute ceilings (path scope, external-effect git/privileged command, protected-branch merge, instruction_patch, parallelism) keep running on top unchanged. The safety argument is a second, stronger boundary, not the absence of the first: decide() never sees a /work path (that translation happens later, in the engine), so the lexical path-scope cap keeps operating on the same host paths as always, redundant with — not replaced by — the Docker mount namespace and the broker's own /work revalidation 0135 Executes decision #5 of the "real container execution" plan, already accepted before this PR existed: the RN-105 image gate — 409 on the Code tab until someone decided artifact.project_image — stops being dispensed for mounted/runner (ADR 0072/RN-169, revised by ADR 0104/RN-421). ReadProjectCodeUseCase.portaoDoContainer drops its executionMode !== 'container' early return; the gate becomes unconditional across all three modes, and ProjectCodeTab (web) stops treating mounted/runner as a special case — same useQuery, same four states, modoLocal branch removed, which SIMPLIFIES the component rather than adding a case. Accepted cost, stated plainly: every EXISTING mounted/runner project without a decided image — including this repo's own dogfooding projects, exp001/exp002 — loses Code-tab access the instant this ships, until the Architect (or Infra's election, ADR 0133) decides one; that is operator action required AFTER deploy, so the branch is breaking/, not bugfix/, even though the change reads as a fix, and the version bump to MAJOR is mechanical, not manual. RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase also drops its 400-by-mode rejection — project_containers can register a row for all three modes now — but investigated and confirmed unchanged: reaching running for real stays impossible for mounted/runner, enforced in exactly one place, ContainerBrokerPort.start()'s ModoDeExecucaoNaoSuportadoError (the broker runs on the SERVER and cannot see the user's folder), which ExecuteContainerStartUseCase already turns into an ordinary container.start_failed — never a crash, never a silent fallback — BEFORE any lifecycle transition is even attempted, so no row is born for those modes through the real approval path despite the 400 being gone. No second mode check was added at the api/propose layer on purpose: duplicating the broker's would-be gate creates a second place to drift from the first, the exact lesson the broker's own comment already recorded while pointing at this ADR. Also investigated, and left declared rather than fixed here (out of this PR's API/domain scope): neither propose_container_start (the Infra Lead's tool) nor GetInfraContextUseCase restrict by executionMode today, so the Infra Lead can still propose container_start for a mounted/runner project — pre-existing gap, wastes one approval cycle, fails loud and named rather than silently 0136 The global containers page (/containers, cross-project) closes the ADR 0130 port comment's other declared gap — "stop/remove have no caller yet" — with two decisions the plan didn't specify. First: the page reads the REGISTERED state in three constant queries (ContainersOverviewRepository, same no-N+1 shape as ProjectsSummaryRepository), but asking the broker for the OBSERVED state is a network call per project — so only provisioning/running rows are eligible, capped at TETO_DE_VERIFICACOES_POR_CARGA (20) per load, in parallel; what falls outside either rule carries its OWN naoVerificado reason, never confused with the broker's own naoObservado (RN-468/486 discipline extended to a new screen). Second: container_stop gets container_start's exact calibre (maintainer, configurable auto-approve, never seeded); container_remove — the only one of the three that discards the container and forces a full reprovision — joins the SAME absolute ceiling as external-effect git/privileged commands (RN-418): never auto-approvable, "always allow" refused at the source. ContainerBrokerPort.remove was already docker rm --force (removes even running, one call); rather than widen the state machine with a running -> removed shortcut, ExecuteContainerRemoveUseCase records the two real hops (stopped, then removed). "Start again" reuses container_start verbatim — zero backend change — building its payload from the project's current image decision instead of a fourth action type 0137 Closes the other half ADR 0135 left declared: mounted/runner now require a decided image (RN-105 gate, all three modes) but still had no way to bring a container up — the server-side broker refuses those two modes outright, because their code lives in a folder only the USER's machine can see. container_start/container_stop/container_remove gain a SECOND execution path, branched by executionMode only at EXECUTION time (never at propose or approve, both still mode-agnostic): container keeps going through the broker unchanged; mounted/runner now ask the ENGINE to relay to the connected RUNNER, over three new event pairs on the same Phoenix channel — container_start/_result, container_stop/_result, container_remove/_result — replicating the exact exec/exec_result pattern rather than inventing a new one. The runner answers with DockerViaCli (@brabo/docker-port), the SAME port the broker uses server-side, proven so far only by --self-test-docker and now with a real caller; the image it starts is READ from the current decision (ObterSpecDeContainerUseCase, the same use case the broker's own spec route already calls, invoked directly since both run in the api process), never re-elected. Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor gained NO new outcome: it already routed every command of a connected runner project to the channel unconditionally (RN-423) — host-vs-container is a decision the RUNNER makes internally (EstadoDoRunner.containerAtivo, tratarExec switching to docker exec with cwd translated by prefix swap, cwdParaContainer). guard.ts's $HOME containment (RN-434) needed zero new code to cover the new mount — verified by reading the file whole: the bind IS estado.dir, the same root already validated at CLI startup, before any channel connects. "No runner connected"/timeout (RunnerNaoConectadoError) and "the runner tried and refused" (RunnerRecusouContainerError) are both ordinary failed outcomes, never an uncaught exception — same discipline as BrokerIndisponivelError/BrokerRecusouError 0143 A real exp001 run had ten dev tasks lock up at once, and the finding was not the particular folder that failed — it was that nothing ordered container before dev agent: no container_start was ever proposed, and ten dev agents started anyway. So Engine.Dev.AgentIo.try_claim/2 — the SINGLE claim point — now asks ProjectContainerLifecycle.running?/1 (the predicate ADR 0134 already introduced, no new machinery) BEFORE calling the api, and without a REGISTERED running row the agent falls to :idle, persists, and emits dev.blocked_by_container. In the ENGINE and not only at the api's activate-execution gate, because claiming has one path no route covers: REHYDRATION does no :work cast — DevAgentServer.init/1 -> finish_restart_recovery/1 -> try_claim/2 claims on its own, so an HTTP-only gate would let every rehydrated agent go back to work containerless, in exactly the situation where nobody is watching. :idle and not a new status, for the reason try_claim/2's own docblock had recorded back in Phase 12b: it is the only state a wake still rescues, and every handle_info/2 guard is keyed to it — a :blocked_by_container would be a state nothing rescues. What distinguishes "the queue emptied" from "there is no container" is the EVENT, never the status. Waking is by outbox: RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase appends container.running in the SAME transaction that records the arrival, under a container aggregate (the third Engine.Outbox.Drain reads, next to session/task) rather than borrowing task to save a query line, with the PROJECT as aggregateId; the delivered message is the EXISTING {:wake, :became_claimable}, whose semantics already are "there may be work now" — a new one would need a new handle_info/2 clause in both servers with an identical guard and no different decision to make. Second half, same rule seen from the other side: TerminalExecutor.decisao_de_execucao/1 stops degrading silently — container with no running container used to fall through to System.cmd INSIDE the engine process, so ADR 0134's isolation held only on the happy path. It now refuses (:recusar_container_ausente), mirroring the runner mode's two existing refusals, with mounted in the same branch, and the catch-all shrinks to what it should always have covered alone: nonexistent project or malformed id. Declared cost, and the reason this can only ship AFTER mounted gets a container: a project without one stops working — loudly, which is the point 0144 A project in Mounted mode could not have a container at all, blocked twice over: ExecuteContainerStartUseCase sent every non-container mode to the RUNNER (which requires a connected brabo-runner), and the broker refused any non-container mode at the source. Both refusals were about GEOMETRY rather than the mode's name — a mounted project's folder sat somewhere arbitrary on the operator's disk that the server's Docker daemon had no reason to see — and ADR 0141 changed exactly that geometry by putting every mounted project under ONE base mounted by identity. So the broker gains a SECOND root, BRABO_PROJECTS_HOST_BASE, and the api starts sending a DISCRIMINATED locator that says which root a segment belongs to: gerenciada (the managed folder, named by workspace_dir_name), montada (the RELATIVE path under the base) or indisponivel (no root here reaches it, with the reason). The ADR 0130 invariant is untouched and is the reason for the shape: what crosses the wire is still only the half the broker's root does not cover, the api never learns where those roots are on the host, and the broker never learns anything about the project — neither side alone can write an arbitrary path, and sending an absolute one would put the containment of a root-equivalent process back in the caller's hands. Three variants and not two because indisponivel has two DIFFERENT fixes — a runner project (fix: the runner, on the other side) and a LEGACY mounted project created outside the base (fix: move the folder) — and a null would send whoever operates to the wrong place half the time; a folder that IS the base lands there too, since <root>/ would mount every mounted project inside one project's container. Neither root ever stands in for the other: whichever is missing is named in the refusal (BaseDeProjetosNaoConfiguradaError, mirroring RaizDeWorkspacesNaoConfiguradaError), because the managed root is named by workspace_dir_name and the base is named by the user, so falling back would mount someone else's code with nothing indicating why. Three barriers stand over the concatenation, not one — the api refuses what is outside the base, packages/docker-port refuses a segment that is not relative (.., absolute, empty, NUL), and raizDeProjetoValidada still runs over root + segment before it becomes a -v. On the api side the branch becomes one of DESTINATION: container and mounted go to the broker, only runner to the runner, and container_stop/container_remove move with container_start necessarily — bringing a container up on the server and then asking the user's machine to stop it would leave running, with no way to stop it, what is running. And mounted ELECTS the image like container rather than reading the current one like the runner path: the broker composes from artifact.project_image, which it FETCHES from the api, so an election not written to that artifact would be inert — the ADR 0133 argument applied to a second mode 0180 The project container runs as the FOLDER'S OWNER (--user uid:gid, measured by the api, revalidated by the broker, never from a request body), so dev agents can write to /work under --cap-drop ALL (AT-247). Adds one field to the spec, opens no containment door 0190 The Infra brings the container up ON ITS OWN when its handoff is accepted (AT-260, owner decision 01/10), revising ADR 0133's "never seeded" without editing it: the accept seeds container_start: auto_approve for the Infra agent, and the Infra Lead's SERVER — not the model, not a new tool — elects the routing candidate covering the most modules (first one on a tie) and proposes container_start before the first model call, through the SAME path as the tool, with the mode/state refusals (RN-566/610) and the no-broker 409 intact. runner keeps container_start_via_runner with approval, container_remove stays in the absolute cap, and the RN-668 closing stays true. Same owner decision (AT-262): the Dev Lead is offered BY THE INFRA, only with the project container running — the Architect's double handoff goes away, and ADR 0053/0085's "the Dev Lead comes from the Architect" changes without being edited 0199 The container's MINIMUM resources are DERIVED from the module_map (AT-261, owner decision 01/10): each module may declare resources (cpus, memoryMb, pidsLimit — all three or none), and container_start with resources omitted — always the case for the server's start on handoff acceptance (ADR 0190) — starts with the SUM over modules, because they all share ONE container. A module without a declaration floors the container at today's default instead of inventing a number; a map with no declarations gives exactly today's default. A sum above the ceiling is 400 to the Architect when the map is created; a request below the minimum is a named failed 0208 The Infra INHERITS the network the Architect declared in artifact.project_image (AT-392, owner decision 02/10): the server start on handoff acceptance and the propose_container_start tool without network use the Architect's egress/none instead of a literal none, and still start without a click; revises ADR 0190 point 3, departs from ADR 0065 §4, and declares the price (egress reaches the host's published ports, ADR 0189).
documents.s: Project container and broker

documents.t: The CLI on the user's machine — its channel, credentials, device keys, distribution, base and service. # decision 0103 apps/runner (new workspace, Node/TS): a CLI that runs on the user's machine, connects to the engine over a new Phoenix channel (/runner, single-use ticket ISSUED BY THE ENGINE) to run an ALREADY-APPROVED agent command in the user's $SHELL, plus an interactive PTY terminal for the Code tab (the engine does pure byte relay). Routing always happens AFTER approval — never a second execution path. With no runner connected, it falls back to the usual System.cmd (ADR 0072 becomes the fallback). The security boundary is NOT sandboxing: it's authentication + the approval pipeline + the user's consent — guard.ts is declared best-effort. Real finding: with no long-lived account token mechanism in the product, the runner replicates the browser login until a real automation token exists 0105 The Personal Access Token (brb_…) closes the backlog item from ADR 0104: apps/runner/src/auth.ts swaps replicated login (password+cookie on disk) for a long-lived, project-scoped token. New personal_access_tokens table, HMAC-SHA256+pepper hash via hashDeToken() (a fix to the backlog, which had said argon2 — wrong for a HIGH-entropy secret). Central decision: the PAT never authenticates outside POST .../runner-ticket, BY CONSTRUCTION — IS_PAT_ROUTE_KEY/@RequirePatAuth() (a third branch in JwtAuthGuard, same pattern as IS_SERVICE_ROUTE_KEY) + a route-level PatAuthGuard, never a branch in the global guard that would let RolesGuard authorize the PAT for any route under the user's role. last_used_at is an unconditional UPDATE in the same validation query — no throttling, which would reject a legitimate reconnection under 5 minutes with a 401 0106 Closes the last ADR 0104 backlog item: tsup bundles apps/runner into a single dist/index.cjs (node-pty as a mandatory external — a native binding, can't be bundled), published as @brabo/runner by its OWN workflow, triggered by the same final tag as release.yml. Real, empirically-tested finding: the obvious fix for the auto-run guard (import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(argv[1]).href) was BROKEN in the exact case this piece exists to enable — process.argv[1] is never realpath-resolved, import.meta.url always is, and npm install -g creates exactly that asymmetry via a symlink; the final fix applies realpathSync to argv[1] before comparing. The version is injected only into CI's disposable checkout (npm pkg set), never committed. Mitigates npm's latest regressing when republishing one of the six orphan tags already in the repo — it publishes under its own dist-tag when the target version is older than the current latest. breaking/ — an operator action (creating the npm Automation Token) is required before publishing works end to end 0112 Standalone binary of @brabo/runner via bun build --compile — companion of ADR 0106, closing the ADR 0104 backlog item explicitly deferred there. node-pty resolves its own native .node addon by a path COMPUTED at runtime, which Bun can't embed statically (proven empirically: the naive build compiles clean and throws at runtime); the fix embeds every file node-pty needs via with { type: 'file' } (the only Bun mechanism that accepts a literal specifier) and re-extracts them to a REAL temp directory at startup, preserving the original relative layout so node-pty's own relative require() calls resolve unmodified. Two bugs found only by running the compiled binary: --external node-pty is required on the bun build command itself (Bun silently bundles the non-compiled fallback's await import('node-pty') otherwise, throwing a misleading error at runtime instead of failing the build), and the ADR 0106 auto-run guard needed a second branch for process.argv[1] being a virtual /$bunfs/root/... path inside a compiled binary. Five-target matrix (linux-x64/linux-arm64/darwin-x64/darwin-arm64/win32-x64), each built on its own native runner; only linux-x64 was validated by real execution in this investigation — the other four, Windows especially, are reasoned through node-pty's source, with their first real execution being the next version tag 0118 Browser-driven runner setup: an Ed25519 key pair generated in the browser (Web Crypto) registers as a new runner_device_keys row, and POST .../runner-ticket accepts its short-lived (≤60s) self-signed EdDSA JWT as a SECOND credential alongside the PAT — additive, never a replacement, and explicitly not the session-JWT dual-auth RN-439 already forbids. A new @Public() route proxies the already-published GitHub Releases binary (5-minute in-memory cache of the asset resolution, never the bytes) instead of building or storing a second copy. The File System Access API writes the configured folder directly in Chromium (binary + config + private device key, three files, one click); everywhere else, two plain downloads are the fallback. Accepted limitation: the browser can't set the Unix execute bit, so chmod +x stays manual. --project/--dir/--token become optional in the CLI when a local config is present. Explicitly rejected in the same session: the runner auto-discovering a local Docker/Kubernetes container and connecting over SSH — would reopen Phase 25b, cut on purpose 0145 runner routed every approved terminal command to the connected CLI once workspace was verified and the runner was connected — never checking for a REGISTERED running container, the same predicate container/mounted already required since ADR 0143. The runner decided host-vs-container internally (ADR 0137), and with no container up it fell through to the raw HOST, silently, the exact fallback ADR 0143 had closed for the other two modes. A second defect, declared open since RN-478: Workspace.ensure!/4 tried LOCAL File.mkdir_p!/git init for a runner project's HOST-only path, which the engine process never had a bind-mount to — the earlier fix only improved the failure MESSAGE, the dev agent still had nowhere to work. So the three preconditions (verified, connected, container running) move into Engine.Runners.RunnerReadiness, shared by TerminalExecutor and by the worktree materialization, which now runs on the ACTUAL user machine over the SAME exec/exec_result channel that already runs approved terminal (Engine.Actions.Workspace.RunnerGit, new) instead of inside the engine process — Engine.Dev.WorktreeManager's four operations branch the same way, and the periodic cleanup job (Engine.Dev.WorktreeCleanup) SKIPS a runner project that isn't ready right now instead of either crashing or treating it as orphaned. The exec protocol gains an optional env field (RN-507) so git fetch's credential (ADR 0056) can travel in the child process's environment on the user's machine — merged onto process.env, never substituted, never sent to docker exec (no env support in packages/docker-port, by design) and never logged. Third finding: container_start also served runner, but its payload (imagem/network/resources/rationale — Infra ELECTS a candidate) never applied there — nothing to elect against, since the broker never reaches a runner project's folder. So container_start becomes exclusive to container/mounted (both via the broker, RN-503), and a new action, container_start_via_runner (schema: only optional rationale), covers runner — its Infra Lead tool checks execution_mode and runner connectivity LOCALLY (no HTTP) before proposing, refusing by name instead of proposing blind, unlike propose_container_start's pre-existing, declared, and still-open gap (RN-494) 0147 Writing into a folder the user picked ANYWHERE on the host has exactly three possible mechanisms — run api/engine natively, keep a live process on the host, or have the browser write via the File System Access API — and only the second is continuous. The brabo-runner already is that process, so rather than shipping a second "mirror" binary it becomes ONE local agent that DECLARES CAPABILITIES (espelho, exec, pty) at connection time, with the server granting only what the project's execution_mode requires: one install, one auth, one revocation. Declared in the join params, because today the join is MUTE on both sides — the runner sends {} and the channel signature literally ignores _params, the role coming from the ticket's kind — and granted by intersection, held in socket.assigns as CONNECTION state and never a table, the same reasoning that keeps containerAtivo client-side and that already lets the :global Registry entry die with the pid. A required capability that was not declared REFUSES THE JOIN, which is the right shape because the runner already treats JoinRecusadoError as fatal-without-retry: an incapable runner must not sit in a backoff loop. Capability goes in the join and not in a post-join push like workspace_confirm because that one describes the WORKSPACE, which changes, while capability describes the BINARY, fixed for the connection. The mirror gets its own scope guard, sibling of guard.ts, reusing the lexical+realpath double pass that already catches a symlink mid-path, and refuses three things: a symlink escaping the destination, a destination CONTAINING the workspace, and a destination INSIDE it — the last two being the same loop with ADR 0141's bind, in opposite directions. One direction, and NEVER --delete: a file removed in the workspace stays in the destination, and the accumulation is the declared cost. It does NOT require Docker, and gets a SEPARATE predicate rather than a RunnerReadiness with a flag — a shared function with a "skip the container" parameter is precisely how the third precondition gets dropped for exec by accident later; the mirror does not need it because that precondition exists to stop a command from falling through to the raw HOST (ADR 0145), and a file copy on the user's machine has no host to fall through FROM. Revocation turns out to be blind in a way the code's own docblock understates: it declares the cut as "no maintainer view", but PATs have five routes and device keys have two — a developer cannot list even their OWN keys, and you cannot revoke what you cannot see. So listing is added, and revoking stops meaning only "no new tickets": it now drops the LIVE channel, which Registry.whereis/1 already makes reachable. Sync is triggered BY EVENT (end of turn, commit) and never by fs.watch, which would be unbounded work triggered by anything — including the mirror's own writes, which is a loop. And the line that shapes all of it: consent to configuration is not approval of an action. The mirror's write does not go through proposed_action because it is not an agent asking to act; it is the system writing to a path the user declared. Doing it as a terminal command would be the opposite — it would land in ADR 0055's path scope, become a queue of routine approvals, and corrode the very ceiling that gives the click its meaning 0151 The runner gains a consented BASE, and folders get created through the channel — a deliberately narrow slice, with the per-MACHINE runner pushed to the next phase. Today the runner has no base: the only root is --dir, and without it the root IS the cwd (index.ts:242-250); estado.dir is one singular path feeding the cwd guard, the pty, cwdParaContainer and workspace_confirm. The base exists only in the api, and that same file forbids in writing (project-workspaces-root.ts:421-438) that the base rule enter caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido, which runs on EVERY read. Decision: the installer consents ONE base, stored locally; each project is a subfolder; the base is never received over the wire — same shape as the broker (ADR 0144), where the root belongs to whoever executes and only the SEGMENT travels. The guard REUSES dentroDoEscopo and the per-SEGMENT loop refusal from espelho-guard.ts:208-233 (/base-outra is NOT inside /base), never a fourth copy of the rule — the precedent is RN-515. New pair workspace_create/workspace_create_result in the exec/exec_result mould, and then the runner sends the workspace_confirm that already exists, so no new write path is born, the engine still does not write the table, and one single route keeps stamping workspace_verified_at. Records a naming precision: workspace.verified does not exist anywhere — the event is project.workspace_verified — and workspace_confirm is UNIDIRECTIONAL (terminal_channel.ex:356-373 answers {:noreply, socket}), so a pair needing a reply cannot be modelled on it. Capability enters the vocabulary only in the session the code enters (RN-514). Own predicate with TWO preconditions, adopting espelho.ex:19-24 literally on why RunnerReadiness never gains a "skip container" flag. Not a proposed_action. Declares the FIVE independent couplings the per-machine runner must cross, one of them a migration and one of them breaking/ 0154 The local agent's identity becomes the MACHINE's, not the project's. The installer already gets close — since RN-531 it downloads the binary, checks it against the signed checksums.txt and installs it with install -m 0755, no manual chmod — and then STOPS, saying so in its own last line: it does not pair the agent, and the device key still comes from the project screen. What blocks it is not the binary but the IDENTITY: service install needs a projectId and a key, and at install time no project exists — no account, no workspace. FASE 29 measured "one runner per project" as imposed in five independent places; re-measuring with arquivo:linha shows three of them need no change at all, and that is this ADR's finding. RunnerSocket.connect/3 authenticates by TICKET, the ticket is requested per project, and the atomic consume happens at join against the topic's project_id — so the topic (terminal_channel.ex:204), the socket id (runner_socket.ex:73) and the ticket describe a CONNECTION, not a process. One process opening N connections, one per project it serves, satisfies all three byte for byte and preserves the refusal of a second runner in the same project, which is a real guarantee rather than an accident. What remains is what genuinely belongs to the process: the credential that requests those N tickets and the unit that keeps it alive. So runner_device_keys.project_id becomes nullable, and NULL MEANS machine — same table, same kid inside the private JWK (RN-475), same revocation; a sibling table was considered and refused because PatAuthGuard finds the public key by kid and does not need to know its species, and two tables would mean two lookups, the second forgotten exactly once. A machine key grants nothing its owning user did not already have: runner-ticket stays per project and authorization is still resolved against the project asked for. The runner DISCOVERS which projects it serves through a new GET runner/projects rather than scanning the base — guessing by folder name is the class of error ADR 0141 refused. The unit becomes one per machine, and the per-project ones keep working, with status SAYING they exist rather than leaving six processes fighting over three projects in silence. Refuses: merging topics into a runner:<userId>, a key crossing users, discovering projects from disk, and any exception in decide.ts — this ADR moves identity, never authority. Declares the cost FASE 29 predicted: revoking now drops the agent for every project on that machine 0174 The runner's standalone binary stops promising the Intel Mac: four targets instead of the five of ADR 0112. Measured (AT-065): macos-13 has no runner (image retired by GitHub, 24h00m01s queued and cancelled on all three tags), and the replacement macos-15-intel schedules and builds but fails --self-test-pty because under Bun the node-pty onData never fires (oven-sh/bun#25822, open) — the same proof passes under Node. Decided by the maintainer: darwin-x64 leaves the matrix and ALVOS_ESPERADOS, the GET /runner-releases/binary proxy refuses it with its own 400 pointing at the npm package, install.sh on darwin-amd64 does not download and says to run npm install -g @brabo/runner, and the browser still detects it but skips the download. scripts/ci/alvos-do-runner.spec.ts ties the four places that enumerate targets together. Way back: a new ADR once Bun ships the fix 0187 The runner's standalone binary stops promising Windows: three targets instead of the four of ADR 0174, in the same mold. Measured in four workflow_dispatch rehearsals (AT-343, runs 36775746724, 36779817686, 36780804339, 36781729045): the binary builds, the usage runs and node-pty loads once the Windows virtual path is recognized, but under Bun the net.Socket over the ConPTY output named pipe ends after the first chunk — even cmd.exe /c echo dies with 0xC000013A (oven-sh/bun#25822 family). Decided by the maintainer: win32-x64 leaves the matrix and ALVOS_ESPERADOS, the GET /runner-releases/binary proxy refuses it with its own 400 pointing at npm install -g @brabo/runner, the install.sh Windows refusal names the npm path, and the browser still detects it but skips the download. Way back: a new ADR once Bun ships the fix 0193 CREDENTIALED git runs on the runner HOST, code runs in the container (AT-116, owner decision 01/10): the authenticated git fetch of RunnerGit goes MARKED (gitCredenciado: true, set only by RunnerRouter.exec_git_credenciado/5) and the runner executes it on the host even with an active container, where the env reaches the child process — the same folder, since estado.dir is the /work bind-mount. No ADR 0130 port changes (DockerPort.exec still has no env), RunnerReadiness stays byte for byte, and the RN-558 refusal shrinks to env WITHOUT the mark (in practice a runner older than this ADR) 0201 Revocation targets the KEY, not the {project, user} pair (AT-013, owner decision 01/10, revising RN-520 over ADR 0154 and ADR 0155). The runner socket ticket records WHICH credential asked for it (credential_kind/credential_id, nullable, Ecto migration in the engine's own schema), the PatAuthGuard hands it down, the socket keeps it in assigns and in its id, and POST /internal/runner/disconnect-credential voids the credential's pending tickets and asks EVERY registered runner whether it was born from it — so another runner of the same user, on a PAT or another key, stays up, and a MACHINE key is one request instead of the pair applied N times. PAT revocation (RN-426/427) now drops its connections too. Two transition pieces keep what used to fall falling: a LEGACY connection (ticket without a credential) drops by the pair within the projects the api sends, and if the engine does not know the route the key revocation falls back to disconnectRunnerOfUser. The pair route stays for member removal (RN-615). The confirm dialogs change wording only (RN-561); the runner does not change 0203 The browser-driven runner setup of ADR 0118 is retired (AT-014, owner decision 01/10, closes BRB-031): the browser no longer generates the key, downloads the binary or writes the folder, and RunnerOnboardingPanel shows the install.sh command instead — the installer already downloads the verified binary, installs it executable (install -m 0755, so no manual chmod +x anywhere) and pairs the machine from the terminal. apps/web/src/lib/runner-bootstrap.ts and POST /projects/:projectId/runner-device-keys are removed (no other caller; BREAKING), while GET/DELETE and the internal machine-key route stay. Project keys registered before keep working and stay revocable. Declared: team installations lose the PAT-less way to pair a second machine, and GET /runner-releases/binary is left without a production consumer, kept as a separate decision
documents.s: The local runner

documents.t: First-party auth, roles and their ceilings, workspace membership, cross-origin hardening and secret envelopes. # decision 0031 Auth in the api's domain: argon2id with fixed parameters, EdDSA access token from a derived key, refresh rotation with family revocation on reuse, lockout keyed on email (not id), and the single invariant that closes off enumeration 0032 The atomic Keycloak cutover: our own issuer in the guard without touching RBAC, /internal/* outside the JWT with a shared secret, web session in an httpOnly cookie with CSRF, and a migrated user indistinguishable from an email that doesn't exist 0037 The CORS the engine didn't have (/health returned 200 and the browser discarded it), its own plug instead of Corsica with /internal and /metrics outside the allowlist, WEB_ORIGIN read in a single place, and strictPort because the port is part of the CORS contract 0050 Credential always encrypted and saved; verification becomes a separate action. ADR 0004's gate (test BEFORE persisting) looked prudent and produced the worst outcome: a write-only field + refusal = a user with no credential AND no text to fix, because the screen never re-shows what they pasted. Storing and verifying are different questions, and tying them together made the second depend on the first having an answer right now. Applies to LLM and git alike — same table, same promise, and treating them differently would give two screens with distinct rules for the same object. The verdict has THREE states because the tester is a NO-OP on ollama/anthropic/openai: with a binary they'd return ok and the screen would claim a verification nobody ran (the ADR 0041 capability rule applied here). A bad key stops being an HTTP exception and becomes a 200 result, so the two @Catch that mapped it went away — a filter that can never fire is dead rule 0058 CSP locked down on the api, and project scope contained at the root. Revises item 7 of 0027, which had decided contentSecurityPolicy: false because "the api serves JSON and the CSP is the web's" — true, but not the point: the alternative to a GENERIC CSP isn't no header at all, it's a SPECIFIC CSP, and for something that only serves JSON the specific one is default-src 'none', which costs zero behavior. Two paths put the api's response outside the web's CSP reach: DIRECT navigation to a route (pasted link, redirect), rendered on the api's own origin, and frame-ancestors, which only applies to the framed document. Outside production the profile loosens only what the /docs Swagger UI needs, under the SAME condition that mounts Swagger — if it ever goes up in production, the CSP follows instead of silently blocking it. The options moved out of the main.ts literal into security-headers.ts for the same reason that already moved cors-origins.ts: at boot they weren't testable, and the proof has to be a real request, because false and a directives object are both "valid config" and only differ in the HTTP response. Along with it comes containing projectId: it arrives from the route parameter already percent-decoded by Express, so ..%2F..%2Fetc became ../../etc and escaped the root — hitting not just reading and WRITING permissions.json but also the scope that AUTHORIZES the terminal via 0055, i.e., the policy pointing at the wrong place. Validation lives where the root is derived, not in each caller, for the same reason the function exists: duplicated checking is checking that one day diverges. Also records the seven CodeQL dismissals with the reason for each — among them js/insufficient-password-hash over an OAuth state HMAC, where there's no password and a slow hash would be a mistake 0059 The key that signs the git OAuth state has no default. Born from one of 0058's dismissals: dismissing js/insufficient-password-hash was right — there's no password there, the "password" is GIT_OAUTH_STATE_SECRET, a server-side HMAC key, and HMAC-SHA256 is the right primitive. What the argument didn't consider is that a server key with a known default value signs nothing, and that was the case: both read points did process.env.GIT_OAUTH_STATE_SECRET ?? 'dev-oauth-state-secret-change-me'. The same failure mode WEB_ORIGIN had already had closed in cors-origins.ts, and worse for two reasons — the value is PUBLIC (it's in the .env.example of an open-source repo, not a weak default, a published secret), and what it protects is the state, the only obstacle to forging the callback of a route that needs to be public: with the key known, anyone can sign {projectId, userId, provider} of their choice and make the callback write, into that payload's project, the git token obtained from the provider. The detail that decides the shape of the fix is that docker-compose.prod.yml supplied the literal as a fallback, so on the REAL error path the variable WAS defined — requiring just "not empty" wouldn't have caught anything, and that's why the example literal is rejected explicitly, along with a 16-character floor that turns the configuration table's ever-present "weak = CSRF" into an actual check. The check runs at BOOT, not on first use: an api that only failed when someone tried to connect git would stand for weeks accepting a state signed with a public key. Resolved into a single function for the RN-092 reason — there were two copies of the same literal, and diverging them would make the callback reject every legitimate state. Deliberate breakage: production with no variable set stops booting, which is the goal and not a side effect. The four sibling secrets of the same compose (AUTH_JWT_SECRET, BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN, CREDENTIALS_MASTER_KEY, SECRET_KEY_BASE) were left declaredly out, in the backlog — closed later by the same rule, with no new ADR, in RN-114 0084 Social login (GitHub/GitLab), revising the backlog from ADRs 0031/0032 — the ban lifted only for this piece, by the product owner's explicit decision. SocialLoginCallbackUseCase ends by calling the SAME EmitirSessaoUseCase as password login — no second session format. The OAuth client is reused (GithubOauthClient/GitlabOauthClient gain buildLoginAuthorizeUrl/fetchIdentity), but the state is NOT: domain/auth/social-oauth-state.ts signs with the SAME GIT_OAUTH_STATE_SECRET key only because the payload is structurally incompatible — a purpose: 'social_login' discriminant checked BEFORE any other field is what keeps a state from git's CONNECTION flow from being accepted here (RN-273), which would be privilege escalation. New social_identities table (migration 0047), keyed by (provider, provider_user_id) — never email/login, which can change owner (RN-276). The callback decides in three steps: identity already known → log in; email matches an existing account AND is provider-verified → link, and while at it verify the account's email if it wasn't already (RN-279); email matches but NOT verified → refuse, account takeover (RN-274); no matching account → provision a NEW passwordless user, reusing the same "pending" state from the Keycloak migration (RN-278) — here the email doesn't need to be verified, because there's no account to protect (RN-275). Reuses the SAME OAuth app as the git connection flow — zero new environment variables —, changing only redirect_uri and scope (minimal, no repo/api) per request; the OPERATOR action of registering the second callback with the provider is what justifies the breaking/ branch. The access token never travels in the URL: session cookies are written in the callback, and the web boot already rebuilds the session on its own 0096 Real SMTP in MailSender, closing the backlog item open since 0032 ("real SMTP stays future config"). nodemailer over plain SMTP transport — a stateful LINE protocol with MIME/STARTTLS/AUTH, unlike the JSON HTTP APIs the rest of the product integrates — behind MAIL_TRANSPORT (log, default including in production, or smtp), selected by a useFactory in AuthUseCasesModule without touching any use case. SMTP_HOST/SMTP_USER/SMTP_PASSWORD/SMTP_FROM follow the RN-114 pattern in production when the mode is smtp, but WITHOUT the public default the four original RN-114 variables had — the bar only kicks in once the operator opts into smtp, validated in SmtpMailSender's constructor (exercised by the useFactory when the provider graph is assembled, same design as CREDENTIALS_MASTER_KEY), not by an eager call in main.ts. Plain-text body, never HTML — the port carries no structure for rich bodies. Investigation found a real gap before implementing: email_verification had no web route at all (verificarEmail existed in apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts with no caller) — /verificar-email (VerifyEmailPage.tsx) closes that, mirroring SetPasswordPage.tsx 0127 ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase.forProject stays projectRole ?? workspaceRole — the project row OVERRIDES the workspace one in BOTH directions, and restricting someone on a sensitive project (workspace developer → project viewer) is a deliberate capability that "the higher of the two" would delete. What lands instead are TWO caps on the write path, refused with 403 and configurable nowhere: nobody downgrades a workspace owner (so a maintainer can no longer lock the owner out of their own project), and nobody downgrades THEMSELVES (undoing needs the very role being given up). The owner is read from workspace_members.role, never workspaces.created_by — created_by is a historical fact that appears in no authorization path, and a cap reading it would shield a creator who already transferred ownership while leaving the current owner exposed. Cap 2 is stated WITHOUT a threshold ("yourself", not "below maintainer"): the threshold version copies a number out of a controller's @RequireRole into the domain and ages silently if the route's minimum changes; the declared price is that an owner demoting themselves to maintainer — reversible — also falls. They live in the USE CASE with the rule in domain/iam/tetos-de-rebaixamento.ts, not in RolesGuard, which authorizes the CALLER against the route and sees neither body (dto.role) nor target; the FORM follows domain/actions/decide.ts (RN-154/RN-418) minus its outcome, since a synchronous human call has no approval queue to fall into. The three OpenAPI descriptions RN-471 declared false ("the higher of this one and what the person already has", "includes whoever inherits access from the workspace") are corrected here. Declared still possible: downgrading another maintainer, self-PROMOTION (unchanged, not opened here), the workspace-level POST which has no cap at all, and self-downgrade through REMOVAL — RemoveProjectMemberUseCase gained no cap, and the premise that removal is always benign is FALSE (it is, when the workspace role catches the fall; it is irreversible self-downgrade when it doesn't). Both removal cases are pinned in tests, the open one included. The web stays out on purpose and for a structural reason: the screen can compute cap 2 but NOT cap 1, since listProjectMembers returns the project-row role and the target's workspace role is out of the client's reach — half a gate would be the second source of role RN-471 warns against; meanwhile the refusal shows, via the mensagemDaApi toast #444 added 0156 The self-downgrade cap reaches the OTHER door: removing your own project_members row. ADR 0127 capped only the write path and left this movement out in writing, pinning it in a test whose name documented the hole — "removal STILL gets to downgrade whoever called it" — and predicting the cost of closing it (RemoveProjectMemberUseCase.execute's signature). This is that next person. Removal does not delete a role, it SWAPS the effective one: projectRole ?? workspaceRole (RN-471) starts resolving through the second term, so a maintainer whose authority came from the project row, viewer in the workspace, dropped to viewer with no way back — restoring is POST :projectId/members, which demands the very maintainer just abandoned; with no workspace role at all, the fall is to NO access. The rule is cap 2, not a new cap: ehAutoRebaixamento compares effective-today against effective-after and never needed to know which route the second arrived by, so remocaoEhAutoRebaixamento DELEGATES to it passing the workspace role as the requested one, reimplementing no comparison. It exists as its own function for the single case the other's signature cannot state — an actor with no workspace role, where "after" is nothing, which is not a Role. Cap 1 gets no counterpart, on purpose: owner is the top of ROLE_ORDER, so removing a workspace owner's project row can only RAISE their effective role — it is in fact the only way to undo the restriction cap 1 forbids creating, and a cap there would refuse only benign movements while making permanent the state ADR 0127 was born to eliminate. Stated without a threshold, like cap 2, and the declared price rides along: self-removal from project owner down to workspace maintainer is reversible and falls too — the one benign movement that used to pass and now refuses. The message is its OWN, because whoever clicked "remove" asked for no role change and deserves the mechanism, not the add phrase. Refuses: an owner cap on removal, a second comparison rule, touching forProject, extending to the workspace scope (whose POST still has no cap and whose member @Delete does not exist), blocking removal of OTHER people who drop, and a client-side gate — MembersSection.handleRemove already surfaces mensagemDaApi in a toast, and computing only the half the screen can compute is the half-gate ADR 0127 refused. Closes BRB-001 0157 The self-movement cap reaches the WORKSPACE upsert, and self-PROMOTION — which ADR 0127 left standing in writing — becomes a breach and closes. AddWorkspaceMemberUseCase was a twelve-line passthrough that never received the actor, on a route requiring owner: the same class of defect as project_members, one scope up and worse, because here there is no level above to catch the fall and no member @Delete at all (measured; ADR 0156 had used the same fact to postpone this). An owner writing themselves viewer lost the whole workspace — every project, the LLM spend that is theirs by RN-060, and the very ability to invite whoever would restore them — with undoing being this same route, demanding the owner just abandoned. The cap does not count owners, by the literal criterion of ADR 0127 ("stated as a clause, it has no number to age"): a count adds a read that can fall out of step with the write, must judge whether a second owner who left the company still counts, and makes the same request with the same body pass today and refuse tomorrow. The stronger argument is that the clause already produces the invariant a count would exist to guarantee — a workspace never ends up with zero owners, because removing the last one would require that owner to do it, which is exactly the refused movement. Cap 1 gets no counterpart here, and it was considered rather than mirrored: unlike removal (ADR 0156), the movement DOES exist — an owner can demote another owner. It is refused because cap 1 is a rule about hierarchy inversion, and @RequireRole('owner') already makes inversion impossible in this scope: whoever can call is never below whoever they touch. Adding it, on top of the missing removal route, would make owner an absorbing state nobody leaves over HTTP — offboarding, ownership rotation and fixing a wrong invite would all need direct database writes, which is the class of state ADR 0127 was born to eliminate, rebuilt with the sign flipped. So demoting another owner STAYS, reversible through the same route by any remaining owner. Self-promotion closes on both association routes. ADR 0127 had recorded it as a capability that stayed ("the caps are about going down"); reopened here, the answer is that both halves are one movement — a person deciding alone what authority they hold — and the upward half is the only one that ESCALATES privilege, which is precisely what that ADR could claim its caps never did. Rewriting the SAME role still passes: an idempotent upsert is not a movement, and refusing it would break seed.ts. The comparison is not copied: it becomes one classifier, autoMovimentoDoProprioPapel, returning the SENSE rather than a boolean, because the caller needs it to pick the message. ehAutoRebaixamento survives as a reading of that classifier — on purpose, not for compatibility: remocaoEhAutoRebaixamento delegates to it, and widening it would make REMOVAL refuse self-promotion too, breaking the benign movement ADR 0156 protected by name. Four messages, one per sense and per scope — nobody who tried to promote themselves reads the downgrade phrase, and nobody capped in the workspace is told to ask a maintainer. Refuses: counting owners, an owner cap in this scope, creating a workspace member @Delete (a new door would need this same cap plus the last-owner judgement), widening the removal door, touching forProject for the third ADR running, and a client gate — there is none to build, since no apps/web caller of this route exists. Declared cost: a legitimate maintainer who needs owner now depends on someone else. Closes BRB-002 0158 The envelope starts saying WHICH master key wrapped it, and that label never decides whether it opens. The runbook's own page states the hole ("The wrapped_dek stored in the database doesn't identify which key wrapped it"), and two defects follow: the middle step of rotation has no progress — whoever interrupts it cannot tell where it stopped, and "is anything still on the old key?" has no SQL answer, only re-running the script for its printed counter — and a wrong key and a corrupt blob land in the same catch, two diagnoses with opposite actions wearing one generic failure. So both envelope tables gain a nullable key_id, always together, since they share the envelope and the script and changing one would leave an estate where the query answers half. The value is the key's fingerprint, HMAC-SHA256(derived key, label) truncated — which answers the open question the activity left ("not a hash of the key, that gives whoever reads the database an offline verification oracle") by measuring rather than assuming: the envelope is AES-256-GCM, which AUTHENTICATES, so testing a candidate passphrase against wrapped_dek was ALREADY a perfect oracle costing one scrypt; testing it against the fingerprint costs the same scrypt. No oracle is created, and no variable is added either — the operator types the fingerprint nowhere, it is a pure function of the key already published, which is what makes the old "one more metadatum to keep in sync" objection true of an arbitrary id and false of a fingerprint. The label is observability, never authority, and that is where this decision departs from the obvious one: decrypt stays byte for byte, and rewrap still decides "already on the current key" by ATTEMPTING. Using the label to skip the attempt was considered and refused for a failure mode of its own — a row labelled "current" whose envelope sits on the old key would be silently skipped, stay out of the re-wrapped count, and step 3 would make it unreadable forever, turning a metadata inconsistency into secret loss. So the label serves three things outside the crypto decision: the progress query (IS DISTINCT FROM, never <>, so NULL counts as pending), the diagnosis when NEITHER key opens, and the stamp rewrap writes beside the new envelope. No back-fill: key_id is born on the next write, existing rows stay NULL meaning "written before this column" and never "on the current key" — with the declared cost that on an existing installation the query only starts meaning something after the first rotation. The api prints the current fingerprint at boot, because a column nobody can compare against anything is useless. Refuses: KMS/HSM/per-tenant keys (ADR 0027 stands), an index on key_id, and moving the diagnosis into the hot read path 0173 Workspace member removal is born, capped by the SAME clause. DELETE /workspaces/:workspaceId/members/:userId (owner, 204) ends offboarding by database write, which ADR 0157 refused to open in passing. Cap 2 is inherited with no new rule — remocaoEhAutoRebaixamento with the workspace role as today's effective role and none as the role after, since nothing above catches the fall — so removing YOURSELF is always 403, and that same clause protects the last owner without counting: only an owner calls the route and nobody removes themselves, so every removal leaves at least the caller. Removing ANOTHER owner is allowed; cap 1 still has no counterpart. The removal cascades in one transaction (the target's project_members rows in the workspace, their project device keys and PATs there) and then drops their live runner per project through the RN-520 path. Declared open: workspaces.created_by does not change, so removing the creator leaves agents spending the creator's LLM key (RN-058).
